new_candidates.date_enacted: 2026-09-09, Trumbull Town Council, unanimous voice vote at a public hearing/regular meeting
new_candidates.legal_basis: Resolution TC31-65 (Trumbull Town Council), amending the Trumbull Municipal Code: 'The Town hereby adopts a two-year moratorium on the establishment and development of any new data centers within the Town of Trumbull.' Public hearing held at the same September 9, 2026 Town Council meeting.
new_candidates.trigger: specific_project concerns: 365 Data Centers (Norwalk) and Aphorio Carter (a data center division of private equity firm Carter Funds) announced in May 2026 plans for a 200 MW pipeline of AI-ready data centers, naming Trumbull's decades-old former Nasdaq data center at 80 Merritt Blvd. as a likely site for modernization into a 'high density, AI-ready' facility; a resident petition and advocacy group (Trumbull AI Data Center Watch) pushed for a moratorium and had sought (unsuccessfully) to have it cover the 80 Merritt Blvd. project itself.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23. The Town Council unanimously adopted Resolution TC31-65 on 2026-09-09, imposing a 2-year moratorium (effective immediately) on the 'establishment and development' of any new data centers in Trumbull. The moratorium does NOT apply to the modernization/upgrade of the town's existing 80 Merritt Blvd. data center (a 15 MW facility in operation 50+ years, now being converted to AI-ready use by 365 Data Centers), which the town characterizes as a renovation rather than new construction; residents have petitioned unsuccessfully to have that project included and are considering a signature drive (requiring roughly 2,400 voters) to force a referendum.
new_candidates.affected_projects: 80 Merritt Blvd. (former Nasdaq data center, 15 MW capacity) -- explicitly excluded from the moratorium's scope as an existing-facility modernization, not a new data center; First Selectman Vicki Tesoro reported the operator (365 Data Centers/Aphorio Carter) agreed to no increase in electrical draw, noise, or water use, and no expansion of the building footprint, as part of ongoing negotiations.
new_candidates.outcome: 2-year moratorium on new data center establishment/development adopted unanimously; does not reach the town's existing (and currently most active) data center project, which continues as a modernization outside the moratorium's scope.

new_candidates.date_enacted: Not yet adopted as of 2026-09-23. Application #26-25 (a text amendment to Cromwell Zoning Regulations Section 4.2.E. to impose a 12-month moratorium on data centers) was introduced by Planning and Zoning Commission Chair Kelly; on 2026-08-18 the Commission voted 5-1 (Commissioner Michael Cannata dissenting) only to accept the application and schedule it for a public hearing at a Special Meeting on 2026-09-24 -- one day after this research date.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Proposed text amendment (Application #26-25) to Cromwell Zoning Regulations Section 4.2.E.; not yet adopted. Public hearing scheduled for a Special Meeting of the Planning and Zoning Commission on 2026-09-24.
new_candidates.trigger: regulatory_gap: the town's zoning regulations have no definition or standards for a data center use; the moratorium proposal was introduced to pause any data center application while regulations are developed alongside a broader, already-contracted zoning-regulations rewrite (consultant IMEG). Commissioner Cannata opposed the moratorium, citing an unnamed prospective applicant who has worked with the town for nine months and already secured a property option.
new_candidates.current_status: Pending as of 2026-09-23. At its August 18, 2026 regular meeting, the Cromwell Planning and Zoning Commission voted 5-1 to accept Application #26-25 (the proposed 12-month data center moratorium text amendment) and schedule it for a public hearing at a Special Meeting on September 24, 2026 -- the Commission did not adopt the moratorium at the August 18 meeting itself. Staff confirmed no data center application is currently pending, though one commissioner referenced an interested prospective applicant. A secondary aggregator (mytownview.com) inaccurately described this August 18 procedural vote as the Commission having 'approved' and 'passed' the moratorium itself; the official filed minutes make clear only the scheduling of a hearing was voted on.
new_candidates.affected_projects: An unnamed prospective data center applicant, described by Commissioner Cannata as having worked with the town for approximately nine months and secured an option on a property, was cited during discussion; no formal application has been filed.
new_candidates.outcome: Planning and Zoning Commission voted 5-1 to schedule a public hearing (Sept. 24, 2026) on a proposed 12-month data center moratorium text amendment; the moratorium itself has not been adopted as of this research date.
